title: Passage from functorial complex resolutions to homotopy derivability
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Use cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms, shifts and mapping cones of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K(A)$ have complexes as objects and cochain maps modulo homotopy $f-g=d h+h d$ as morphisms, and let $q:\mathrm{CoCh}(A)\to K(A)$ be the quotient. Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of objects of $K(A)$ closed under isomorphisms, containing zero and stable under all integer shifts and mapping cones. Equivalently its full subcategory is triangulated: in any triangle isomorphic to a mapping-cone triangle, membership of two vertices implies membership of the third. Suppose there are a functor $\rho:\mathrm{CoCh}(A)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(A)$ and a natural transformation $p:\rho\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}$ such that every $p_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\mathcal P(q\rho L)$ holds for every complex $L$. Then the full inclusion $K(A)_{\mathcal P}\to K(A)$, equipped on both sides with quasi-isomorphisms, is a left derivability structure [def-sfb-left-derivability-structure]. Only functoriality on complexes is assumed; no functor on $K(A)$ induced by $\rho$ is required.
